## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A three-fascicle verse rendering of the **Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya**, composed by the Indian author **Viśākha** ([毘舍佉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%98%E8%88%8D%E4%BD%89) — same person as [勝友](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8B%9D%E5%8F%8B) in [KR6k0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0039), the two Chinese names being transliteration and translation respectively of the Sanskrit *Viśākha*). Translated by **Yìjìng** ([義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8)) in the early 8th century.

**Abstract**

The *Vinaya-pīta* / verse-Vinaya genre — versified summaries of the rule-content of the parent Vinaya — was a standard pedagogical form in late-Indian Buddhism, designed to facilitate memorisation. Viśākha's verse-Vinaya is the only extant Mūlasarvāstivāda example of this genre in Chinese, and serves as a complement to his prose *Vinaya-saṃgraha* ([KR6k0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0039)). The two together constitute the **Vinaya-mūlasarvāstivāda** scholastic apparatus available in 8th-century India and brought back by Yìjìng.
